question: Are customers describing the same underlying problem in different ways?

answer.answer_markdown:
**Yes, and it is the single biggest reason a keyword report understates a problem: 7417 extracted topics across 5425 contacts collapse into just 222 distinct themes, because customers describe the same underlying failure in words that share almost no vocabulary.**

The clearest case is the largest theme in the book, *Fraud and dispute claims denied despite evidence*. It covers 379 contacts, 7.0% of everything, spread over 6 products, and the customers reach it through 381 distinct wordings. Three of those wordings, all filed under the same theme:

- "Multiple branch managers and supervisors refused to review the ATM's video footage to confirm what happened."
- "About $7,000.00 in charges made after a gaming site reactivated a self-excluded account without consent were mostly denied by Chase as voluntary despite submitted evidence."
- "After receiving a fabric shelf instead of an air purifier and a replacement being sent, I was charged for a second item I never received, and Chase would not reverse it."

Video footage, an online gaming self-exclusion, and a fabric shelf delivered instead of an air purifier. No search term connects them. Yet the underlying failure is identical in all three: the customer supplied evidence, and the bank's dispute process decided without weighing it.

The same thing happens on the second largest theme, *Unexplained account closures or restrictions*, which covers 353 contacts, 6.5% of everything, in 364 distinct wordings across 5 products. One customer writes only "Her savings account was closed without any warning.", while another describes something that reads like a different product entirely: "Chase says the customer has a permanent EWS restriction blocking a service but will not disclose details or how to resolve it.". Two sentences with no shared words, one operating failure, which is that the bank acts on an account and will not say why.

This is not confined to the top two. The themes with the widest range of phrasing together cover roughly two contacts in every five in the whole book. The practical consequence for the contact centre is that counting keywords, or counting the reason codes agents pick, will always split these problems into fragments too small to fund a fix; grouping by the described failure is what makes them big enough to act on.

charts.title: Themes by number of distinct customer wordings

caveats: The book mixes two corpora: 4425 real written complaints about one bank (July 2024 to June 2026) and 1000 synthetic agent/customer phone conversations from September 2023. Both are counted in every unfiltered number here.
Written complaints are long and self-edited, so they carry more distinct phrasing than a short phone call; the wording counts are therefore driven mainly by the complaint corpus.

Themes are produced by a model grouping issue statements, not by a human taxonomy. Each theme carries a grouping quality flag and the two shown here are marked ok, but the grouping has not been independently audited.
theme_detail returns a sample of the distinct wordings, not all 381 or 364 of them.

payload.name: list_themes
payload.summary: 15 rows over 5425 calls in scope; Fraud and dispute claims denied despite evidence (379), Unexplained account closures or restrictions (353), Contradictory information from bank representatives (281)

sql.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

SELECT th.theme_id, th.name, th.problem_statement, th.root_cause, th.polarity, th.driver_category, th.n_wordings, th.n_products, COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') AS grouping_quality, th.first_seen_week, es.status AS status_at_as_of, es.emerging_score, COUNT(DISTINCT s.call_id) AS n_calls, SUM(CASE WHEN s.min_sentiment < 0 THEN -s.min_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS neg_mass, SUM(CASE WHEN s.max_sentiment > 0 THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS pos_mass, AVG(CASE WHEN th.polarity = 'positive' THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE s.min_sentiment END) AS mean_sentiment FROM themes th JOIN v_theme_call_sentiment s ON s.theme_id = th.theme_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = s.call_id LEFT JOIN emerging_scores es ON es.entity_type = 'theme' AND es.entity_id = th.theme_id AND es.as_of_week = ? WHERE 1=1 AND th.status = 'active' AND COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') != 'weak' GROUP BY th.theme_id HAVING n_calls >= ? ORDER BY th.n_wordings DESC, th.theme_id LIMIT ?
SELECT tc.theme_id, tc.call_id FROM v_theme_calls tc JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = tc.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND tc.theme_id IN (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ORDER BY c.date DESC, tc.call_id

SELECT t.driver_category, COUNT(DISTINCT t.call_id) AS n FROM theme_members tm JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = tm.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1 GROUP BY t.driver_category ORDER BY n DESC
SELECT t.driver, t.call_id FROM theme_members tm JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = tm.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1
SELECT w.rank, w.issue_statement, w.call_id, w.date, w.product FROM theme_wordings w JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = w.call_id WHERE w.theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY w.rank LIMIT 12
SELECT c.product AS value, COUNT(*) AS n_slice FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY value
SELECT c.product AS value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.call_id) AS n FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY value
SELECT DISTINCT c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ?
SELECT c.channel AS value, COUNT(*) AS n_slice FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY value
SELECT c.channel AS value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.call_id) AS n FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY value
SELECT DISTINCT c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ?
SELECT c.week AS period, COUNT(*) AS n FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY period ORDER BY period
SELECT c.week AS period, c.call_id FROM calls c JOIN v_theme_calls x ON x.call_id = c.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND x.theme_id = ? GROUP BY period, c.call_id

SELECT m.from_theme, f.name AS from_name, m.into_theme, m.pass, m.reason, m.judged_by, m.created_at FROM theme_merges m JOIN themes f ON f.theme_id = m.from_theme WHERE m.into_theme = ? OR f.effective_theme_id = ? ORDER BY m.created_at, m.from_theme
SELECT * FROM emerging_scores WHERE entity_type = 'theme' AND entity_id = ? AND as_of_week = ?
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

SELECT e.evidence_id, e.call_id, c.date, c.month, c.product, c.region, c.region_group, c.channel, c.segment, t.sentiment, e.quote, e.speaker, t.topic_label, t.driver, e.char_start, e.char_end, e.match_kind FROM evidence e JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = e.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id JOIN theme_members tm ON tm.topic_id = t.topic_id WHERE e.verified = 1 AND tm.effective_theme_id = ? AND 1=1 ORDER BY ABS(t.sentiment) DESC, c.date DESC, e.evidence_id
